title: The finite smooth trace is the scalar extension of the prime-power trace
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-pur-conventions], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $e\geq1$ be the ramification index, defined by $\ell\mathcal O_E=\varpi_E^e\mathcal O_E$. Let $r\geq1$, put $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$ and $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^r\mathcal O_E=A_{E,er}$, where the last identification uses $(\ell^r)=(\varpi_E^{er})$. The map $A\to B$ is finite free [lem-coef-finite-free-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the finite constructible finite-Tor categories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the compact-support functors [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the normalized finite smooth traces [def-pur-smooth-trace]. Write $T_A=A_X(d)[2d]$, $T_B=B_X(d)[2d]$ and $t_A:Rf_{!,A}T_A\to A_Y$, $t_B:Rf_{!,B}T_B\to B_Y$ for the unit-coefficient smooth traces. For every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, let
$$c_{B/A,M}:(Rf_{!,A}M)\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,B}(M\otimes_A B)$$
be the finite-free compact-support coefficient map, obtained by extension by zero followed by the proper direct-image tensor comparison, or equivalently by the compact-support projection map for $B$ [def-exchange-projection]. Under the canonical identifications $T_A\otimes_A B\cong T_B$ and $A_Y\otimes_A B\cong B_Y$, one has the equality of morphisms
$$t_B\circ c_{B/A,T_A}=t_A\otimes_A1_B.$$
Thus the normalization of the finite smooth trace over $B$ is exactly the tensor extension of the normalized prime-power trace, including its sign and Tate twist.

proof.text: Write $S_T=-\otimes_A^LB$. Apply [lem-coef-finite-free-extension] to $\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E$ and level $r$: it gives the finite-free ring $B=A_{E,er}$, because $(\ell^r)=(\varpi_E^{er})$, including for ramified $E$. Scalar extension preserves the bounded constructible finite-Tor domain and its Tor interval by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Its intrinsic constructibility convention is exactly [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], hence the convention in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Ordinary and pro-etale constructible realizations agree by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin].

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text: The twist construction [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] identifies $S_TA_T(d)=B_T(d)$: its balancing map on the common roots-of-unity tower is $(z\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto z\otimes ab$, and tensor powers give $d\geq0$. These twists are locally free of rank one by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]; thus $T_A,T_B$ have finite Tor amplitude and no additional derived tensor terms occur. Shifts commute with $S$. The actual etale/pro-etale twist identifications and normalized integration maps are those of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], so its common exponent $\ell^r$ gives the same twists as in the coefficient-transport results below. Every finite-type $k$-scheme used here is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field has only the ideals $0,k$.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text: Fix a compactification $f=pj$. The proper coefficient comparison in [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] is the counit transpose for a finite $A$-algebra $B$, while [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] and [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] identify the open tensor map and preserve the constructible Tor interval. Using [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] on the compactification and [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] for the etale-origin witness, the composite is the specified $c_{B/A,M}$; by [def-exchange-projection] its restriction is the compact-support projection transformation.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons] to the finite-free extension $A\to B$. It identifies the exceptional comparison $b_{h,L}:S_VG_{h,A}L\to G_{h,B}S_WL$ as the adjoint mate of $S\epsilon_Ac^{-1}$ and states the counit equation $\epsilon_{h,B,S_WL}P_{h,B}(b_{h,L})c_{h,G_{h,A}L}=S_W(\epsilon_{h,A,L})$. Taking $h=f$ gives $(*)$ and fixes the actual comparison by uniqueness of the adjunction transpose; no unrestricted pro-etale adjunction is used.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-finite-free-projection-exchange] to the same extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E$. It identifies the actual proper and compact-support projection maps, the compact-support exchange, and their open constituents under $S$ and $c$. The maps in that lemma and the preceding construction are identical: both use the proper counit transpose and the open balancing map. When an inverse exchange is used, it exists by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]; all objects have etale-origin witnesses by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. An equality of invertible comparison squares also identifies their inverses.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text: Let $h=f$ and, for $R=A,B$, let $C_{R,L}=\lambda\circ(\epsilon_{h,R,R_W}\otimes1)\circ\operatorname{PF}^{-1}_{h,R;\omega_{h,R},L}\circ\sigma$ be the composite whose $F_R\dashv G_R$ transpose is $\theta_{h,R,L}$ in [def-pur-co-smoothness] ($\sigma$ symmetry, $\lambda$ unitor). First, for any $a:P_{h,A}M\to L$ with transpose $a^\flat=G_{h,A}(a)\eta_{A,M}$, $b_{h,L}S_V(a^\flat)$ is the $B$-transpose of $S_W(a)c_{h,M}^{-1}$: by the counit equation of [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons] (Step 4) and naturality of $c$, $\epsilon_BP_B(b_L)P_B(S a^\flat)=S(\epsilon_A)c^{-1}P_B(Sa^\flat)=S(\epsilon_AP_A(a^\flat))c^{-1}=S(a)c^{-1}$. Hence it suffices that $S(C_{A,L})=C_{B,SL}\,P_B(1\otimes b_{h,A_W})\,c$. Invert the projection equation of [lem-pur-finite-free-projection-exchange] (Step 5): $S(\operatorname{PF}_A^{-1})=(c_\omega\otimes1)^{-1}\operatorname{PF}_B^{-1}c$; the inverses exist by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], whose hypotheses hold because $\omega_{h,A}$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor by [thm-sf-preservation-class]. Then the counit equation at $L=A_W$, $S(\epsilon_A)c_\omega^{-1}=\epsilon_BP_B(b_{A_W})$, naturality of $\operatorname{PF}_B$ in its first variable along $b_{A_W}$, and naturality of $c$ and $\sigma$ give the required identity. Transposing, after tensor reassociation, $b_{h,L}S_V(\theta_{h,A,L})=\theta_{h,B,S_WL}(1\otimes b_{h,A_W})$.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text: At the prime-power model, [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] gives the unit-and-Kummer decomposition and defines the normalized trace as the second projection of its inverse. The finite-free adjoint comparison [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons], together with the twist and Kummer scalar identifications in [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], transports this decomposition and its counit to $B$; uniqueness of the adjoint mate gives $c_qS_S(b_{q,A})=b_{q,B}$ and therefore $t_{q,B}c_q=S_S(t_{q,A})$. The site comparison and open-counit compatibility in [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] carry this equality to the affine-line restriction used by the normalized integration maps.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text:
For composable separated finite-type maps use [lem-pur-finite-free-compact-composition]. With $\alpha_R:P_{g,R}P_{h,R}\cong P_{gh,R}$ its equation is
$$c_{gh,K}\,S(\alpha_{A,K})=\alpha_{B,SK}\,P_{g,B}(c_{h,K})\,c_{g,P_{h,A}K}.$$
Its refinement equation shows that this is the canonical compactification comparison, including for the product compactifications by projective lines used in the coordinate tower. This supplies the geometric-composition equation separately from the counit equation $(*)$.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text: Induct on the ordered coordinate rank in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. Rank zero is the identity adjunction and its trace equation is the identity. For rank $m+1$ write $\mathbf A^{m+1}_S\xrightarrow a\mathbf A^m_S\xrightarrow{p_m}S$, with $a$ the final affine-line projection. Its right adjoint is $a^*(-)(1)[2]$. The counit at $K$ is the open restriction of inverse projection followed by $1_K\otimes t_q$ [def-amb-p1-trace]. The projection equation of Step 5 and the projective-line equation of Step 7 identify this counit under $S$, also at $K=R_{\mathbf A^m}(m)[2m]$. The inverse projection exists by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], since that coefficient is a shifted locally free line. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] the composite counit is $\epsilon_{p_m,R,R_S}\,P_{p_m,R}(\epsilon_{a,R,G_{p_m,R}R_S})$. Substitute the inductive trace equation and this affine-line equation; naturality of $c$ and the composition equation of Step 8 give $t_{p_{m+1},B}c=S(t_{p_{m+1},A})$. This establishes the induction. The site comparison [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] identifies these with the actual pro-etale maps. All interchanged shifts are even: $(-1)^{2m\cdot2}=1$.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text: For a rank-$d$ vector bundle $\pi:V\to S$, [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] characterizes its integration as the unique map with the specified traces on trivializing opens. By Step 5 coefficient extension commutes with the exchange used for each such restriction. Thus $S(t_{\pi,A})c^{-1}$ restricts to the $B$-affine-space trace by Step 9, and uniqueness gives $t_{\pi,B}c=S(t_{\pi,A})$. This uniqueness is valid for these maps because [def-amb-vector-integration] glues degree-zero sheaf morphisms, rather than arbitrary derived morphisms. By [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] the inverse orientation of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] is the adjoint transpose of this integration. The counit equation $(*)$ identifies its scalar extension with the $B$-transpose. The $B$-adjunction bijection is injective, so this is compatibility of the specified normalized vector-bundle orientation.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text:
Put $W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion], this is a closed regular section of $p_1$ with normal bundle $T_{X/Y}$ of rank $d$. The canonical construction of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] has the three arrows
$$\alpha_{f,R}:\omega_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_R(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\delta_R}C_R(\pi_T,0_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X(d)[2d].$$
Here $C$ is [def-pur-section-invariant]; the first arrow is the inverse section identification of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], the middle one is the normalized DNC comparison of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and the last is zero-section pullback of the normalized vector orientation. This writes out the construction whose coefficient compatibility is at issue.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text:
Use [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport] with its prime ring $R=A=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ and target $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^r$. Its categories are the same intrinsic bounded constructible finite-Tor categories as here, and its etale Tate lines identify with the prescribed twists by Step 2. Its exceptional comparison is counit-characterized; [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] gives the same transpose $S\epsilon_Ac^{-1}$ as $(*)$. Thus its $c_g$ equals our $b_g$ by uniqueness of the $B$-adjoint. Its section comparisons are consequently $q_{g,s}=s^*b_g$, with the canonical pullback/tensor comparison. The stated DNC equation gives
$$\delta_B\,q_{p_1,\Delta}=q_{\pi_T,0_T}\,S(\delta_A).$$
It also states compatibility with the dualizing base-change exchange and total-space etale localization of pairs. Hence the first arrow of the chain commutes with $S$ and $b$. This uses that lemma's statement, including its standard-coordinate normalization, in place of an inline etale-coordinate or derived-locality argument.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text:
The last arrow of the chain commutes with coefficient extension by Step 10 and the zero-section twist identification of Step 2. Compose this equation, the DNC equation of Step 12 and the first-arrow equation there. Functoriality gives
$$\alpha_{f,B}\circ b_{f,A_Y}=S_X(\alpha_{f,A}),$$
under $S_YA_Y=B_Y$ and $S_XT_A=T_B$. This is the specified diagonal orientation: the middle arrow is the uniquely identity-normalized deformation map, and the endpoint is the integration-normalized vector orientation.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text:
Write $g_R=\gamma_{f,R_Y}:T_R\to G_{f,R}R_Y$. The definition [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] writes it as twist reassociation, tensor with $\alpha_{f,R}^{-1}$, then the canonical tensor map $\theta$. Step 2 identifies the twist reassociation under $S$, Step 13 identifies $\alpha^{-1}$ (functors preserve inverses), and Step 6 identifies the tensor map by its defining adjoint. For that map the input is the degree-zero coefficient unit; the inverse projection formula in its definition exists by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. Its hypotheses hold since $\omega_{f,R}$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor by [thm-sf-preservation-class], and $R_Y$ has Tor interval $[0,0]$; etale-origin witnesses exist by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Functoriality now gives the precise equality
$$g_B=b_{f,A_Y}\circ S_X(g_A):T_B\longrightarrow G_{f,B}B_Y.$$
Thus the actual normalized purity map, rather than an unspecified purity isomorphism, is the coefficient extension under the canonical exceptional comparison.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: finite coefficient compatibility and finite coefficient-field extension; diagonal/DNC and affine-line normalization.

proof.text:
Finally expand the two smooth traces using [def-pur-smooth-trace]: $t_R=\epsilon_{f,R,R_Y}\circ P_{f,R}(g_R)$. Naturality of $c$ at $g_A$ and Step 14 give
$$\begin{aligned}
t_Bc_{T_A}
&=\epsilon_{f,B,B_Y}\,P_{f,B}(b_{f,A_Y})\,P_{f,B}(S_Xg_A)\,c_{T_A}\\
&=\epsilon_{f,B,B_Y}\,P_{f,B}(b_{f,A_Y})\,c_{G_{f,A}A_Y}\,S_Y(P_{f,A}g_A)\\
&=S_Y(\epsilon_{f,A,A_Y})\,S_Y(P_{f,A}g_A)\\
&=S_Y(t_A)=t_A\otimes_A1_B.
\end{aligned}$$
The third line is exactly $(*)$ of Step 4. Every arrow in this calculation is in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, with the specified coefficient-unit and Tate identifications. The rank-one normalization was fixed by the Kummer class, all further shifts were even, and the DNC comparison was fixed by its identity normalization, so this proves the asserted sign and twist normalization as well as the equality. It also covers $d=0$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and the empty source (all relevant source objects are then zero).
